rationale: Shared.state introduces storage places/lookup and shared.syntax introduces field expressions. Resolve.variable reads a nonempty variable; Resolve.field recursively resolves its base and requires the intermediate object's data and a nonempty field. Its output mode is precisely Mode.join of base access and stored field mode: unique only for two unique operands, otherwise shared. No rule changes storage or resolves an empty/missing intermediate slot. The final object need not be independently looked up by Resolve; the text carefully refers to intermediate objects, and well-formedness supplies target allocation later.
limitations: This review compares semantic intent and formal statements; it does not independently re-prove Lean theorems or audit proof tactics.

Association lists represent raw states and class tables; finite-map prose uses the documented distinct-key/well-formedness conventions. Conservative whole-source snapshots not listed as examined serve freshness only.
